summary: Robert E. Morrell worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and teacher William H. McCullough, and held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

Robert E. Svoboda works in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Oklahoma (~1970–1972) and under mentor Vimalananda (~1975–1983). In 2008, he was an adjunct member at The Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.

Robert F. Rhodes specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He was a Ph.D. candidate at Harvard University, served on a committee for the Otani Academic Society (attested 2000), and was a professor at Otani University (attested 1993–1997 and 2012–2014).

Robert Florida is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and was an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).
Robert Ford Campany specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He was a professor at Indiana University (~1989–2006) and held a post at Vanderbilt University (~2010).

Robert Gardner earned a BA from Harvard University (~1943–1947), founded Harvard University in 1957, and served as a professor there (1956–1997). He also worked at the Fogg Museum and taught medieval art and history at the University of Puget Sound.

Robert Gauthiot was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1900–1906) and became a member of the Société Asiatique in 1909.
Robert Göbl was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (1947–1950) and later held a post there (~1955–1989).

Robert H. Brower was a Japanology scholar who studied at Harvard (~1940–1944) and Michigan (~1945–1947). He taught at Minnesota (1951–1954), Stanford (1954–1966), directed the Inter-University Center (1963–1964), and chaired Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).

Robert H. Sharf specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Toronto, Kyoto, and Michigan (PhD ~1981–1991), and held posts at McMaster, Kyoto, Michigan, and UC Berkeley, where he was named D. H. Chen Distinguished Professor (~2003).
Robert Hinde studied at St John's College (~1941–1948) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1948–1950). He subsequently held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1950–1994).
Robert Hyde Colebrooke worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He was a member of The Asiatic Society (1785–1802) and served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India (1794–1808).
Robert J. Miller worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1955–1988) and at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Robert Kritzer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini (attested 1995) and served as an Associate Professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).
Robert Kyd studied at the University of Edinburgh and founded the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden in 1787.

Robert L. Brown specialized in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a curator in South and Southeast Asian art at LACMA (~1980–2014) and served on the Buddhist Studies faculty at UCLA (~1987–2014).

Robert Lenz studied at the University of Tartu and the University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He taught at Tallinn Cathedral School and the University of Breslau, and became Professor des Sanskrit at the University of Saint Petersburg (~1835–1836).

Robert M. Gimello specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, earning his PhD from Columbia (~1968–1976). He served as department head and professor emeritus at the University of Arizona (~1981–2000) and professor at Harvard (~2001–2006).

Robert Maclagan studied history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering, and served as Principal of IIT Roorkee (1847–1860).

Robert Magliola works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD at Princeton (~1966–1970). He held posts at Purdue, Tamkang University, Assumption University, National Taiwan University, and Columbia University.
